Subject: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - Hosted API vs Current Provider - Post-call recap & next steps

Hi Samir / Kara —

Thanks again for the call today — good conversation. Quick recap of the performance / SLO items we covered and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned: 

Summary of current ask:
- Goal: agree end-to-end p95 and p99 latency targets for the core chat/QA path (including network hop to your app).
- Typical workload shape: sustained concurrency ~200 RPS, bursts to ~500 RPS; 8-12 token per response on average; streaming token-by-token output required for UI.

Current provider (what you mentioned on the call):
- p95: ~380 ms (end-to-end, reported)
- p99: ~1.8 s

Redwood hosted hypotheses / baseline (what we believe we can provide):
- Target p95 <= 150 ms end-to-end for your sample prompts (chat path).
- Target p99 <= 350 ms end-to-end under sustained load, with graceful tail behavior during short bursts.
- Streaming: full token-level streaming supported, with first-token latency within p95 targets for standard prompts.

Open clarifications we need from Finlytics:
1) Please confirm whether your p95/p99 numbers include client-side processing (i.e., from when your UI issues the request) or are measured at the provider edge.
2) Provide example prompt shapes, average output token counts, and rate profile (per-minute RPS).
3) Any IP whitelisting / VPC details we need for perf testing or if you'd prefer workload routed through your staging environment.

Proposed next steps:
- I will share our SLO template and a short latency/benchmark chart (attached) for your review.
- Marissa will propose a perf-run plan and initial test harness we can run against your staging endpoints.
- Aim to run an initial performance validation the week of Jun 22.

Please reply with the sample prompts and confirmation on measurement boundaries (client vs provider). If that looks right, we’ll lock in times for the perf run.

Thanks,
Laura

Subject: Re: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - Hosted API vs Current Provider - Post-call recap & next steps

Laura — thanks for the clear summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Our current numbers are measured end-to-end from the browser (so include our client-side overhead and our edge). We can also share provider-side metrics if that helps isolate differences.
2) Prompts: main UI has three patterns — short chat (avg 10 tokens out), summary job (avg 60 tokens), and rerank flow (very short, ~3 tokens). The workload you saw today was dominated (~70%) by the short chat path.
3) Concurrency: sustained 200 RPS during business hours, but we’ve seen bursts up to 600 RPS (very spiky). For the perf run we can simulate sustained 200 and a burst to 600 for 60s.
4) Streaming: yes, token-level streaming is required for the chat UI. At a minimum we need first-token within p95 target and continuous tokens streamed thereafter.

We’re happy to run a small provider-only measurement and share raw logs. Can you confirm whether Redwood’s p95/p99 claims are measured at the provider edge or end-to-end? If provider-edge only, we’ll want to translate to end-to-end with our network/edge numbers.

On next steps: we can provide a staging endpoint and a set of sample prompts (I’ll attach a CSV with the prompt shapes). Also, whitelisting — we’ll need your public egress IPs to allow traffic from your perf harness.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering | Finlytics

Hi all — following up with an initial data point and proposed plan. Attaching a short benchmark chart and our SLO template for your review. 

Initial benchmark (internal test harness, US-west region, public-hosted config, sample chat prompts approximating your short-chat shape):
- Measured provider-edge p95: 120 ms
- Measured provider-edge p99: 320 ms
- First-token latency: ~90 ms p95
- Sustained throughput: validated at 250 RPS on a single pool with consistent tail behavior; we’ve seen stable burst handling to 600 RPS with autoscaling and queueing policies in place (config dependent).

Notes / caveats:
- These were provider-edge measurements. If you measure end-to-end from the browser, add your average network/edge delta (typically 40–80 ms depending on region and proxying).
- VPC / Private deployments may add variability depending on NAT/egress paths. We can run the perf harness directly against your staging endpoint to measure end-to-end.

Proposed perf-run plan:
1) We’ll run a provider-edge validation using the sample prompts you share (short chat + summary + rerank mix).
2) Next, run an end-to-end test against your staging endpoint (requires whitelisting our perf IPs).
3) Capture full traces and token-level streaming logs (we’ll share a short tracing guide).

If that works, Laura — can you propose a 2-hour window the week of Jun 22 for the initial provider-edge run? Samir — once you send the prompt CSV and whitelist info we’ll schedule the staging run.

Thanks,
Marissa
